provenance.note: Initial constants: values marked in `free` are fitted by tools/glm_runner_sim.py calibrate; the rest are read directly from the traces. Nothing here is a quality claim.
provenance.derivation: Per slot the traced cuda-primary step shows cpu_service 0.664 ms and exposed wait 0.258 ms, a period of 0.92 ms set by the primary GPU chain (launch + mixer + publish + residents); the CPU kernel itself is 0.457 ms (CPU_EXPERT) and the worker exposure about 0.1 ms. Single-GPU rows at 2.3x the CPU bytes decode no slower, and the faster HIP card alone decodes 12% faster: decode is bound by the primary GPU chain. The per-slot nsys decomposition (probe 1) must confirm the chain composition.
provenance.per_slot_seed: STEP_TRACE_SLOTS of the cuda-primary trace: KDA slot periods (service+wait) 0.6-0.97 ms, MLA 0.9-1.5 ms; the GPU chain per slot is seeded at 0.80 (KDA) and 1.03 (MLA at 8K) before the fit.

hit_curve.note: scale>1 reflects REAP224 + adaptive worker cache + affinity 0.14 concentrating routes beyond the q23 LRU curve; fitted

acceptance_by_position.source: MTP_POSITION of the timed trial of the cuda-hip 8K trace; positions 3-4 are assumptions

model.note_rows: MIXED_CLIENT decode_rows/requests = 7.3 rows per request at width 2 against ~6.9 worker experts: most experts are routed by one of the two tokens

tr16_8k.source: MTP_POSITION of the timed cuda-hip 8K holdout-code trial (REAP-224 draft head, shipped format); positions 3-4 extrapolated. Same numbers as acceptance_by_position.

llamacpp_q4_full288.source: llama.cpp PR #27917 (superseded by #29928): full 288-expert NextN head at Q4, 3474/4664 drafts accepted, mean length 4.13, CPU-offloaded setup; prompt mix unknown, so this is a prior for the A/B, not a TR16 measurement

model.draft_step_reference_note: draft_step_ms was fitted on 8K traces; the context part moves at mla_kv_ms_per_ktoken (the draft block is a sparse MLA layer with its own indexer) unless draft_context_ms_per_ktoken is set per device
model.mtp_prime_state_note: assumption: a state-only MLA pass (latent kv + indexer keys, no queries, attention, output, MoE or head) costs ~35% of the prefill MLA mixer; replace with MTP_PRIME ms once measured

single15.source: CPU_EXPERT bytes/layer_flow_ms of the trace (375.6 GB / 5723 ms); flow probe 69.8 at width 1-2
single15.note: flow bench interleaved 15 threads 75.7/75.2 GB/s (width 1/2) on 2026-10-14; in-run effective 65.6 GB/s from CPU_EXPERT

node8.source: ram-cpu0-mem0 / ram-cpu1-mem1 probes (42.55/41.65) with 8 threads; a node-local expert lane is not yet measured
node8.note: Not measured: strata-glm-q2-flow-bench refuses a single-node membind (node-owned rows); 42 GB/s is the plain-read probe per node

worker.source: MIXED_CLIENT decode_wait 4353 ms / ownership_wait 2453 ms / 351 updates over 26376 requests; MIXED_WORKER elapsed 0.43-0.49 ms per request
worker.note_return: MIXED_CLIENT prefill_rows 1032192 over 2 passes x 42 layers = 12288 rows per layer at 8192 tokens
worker.note_tile: STRATA_GLM_MIXED_PREFILL_TILE=512: worker GEMM rows per expert are padded to the tile (8192 tokens: 293 -> 512; 2048: 73 -> 512)
worker.note_client: Primary service-thread work per worker request (request packing, ownership memcmp, reply unpacking); seeded, fitted
worker.note_ownership: MIXED_CLIENT ownership_wait_ms / adapt_updates: 7.0 ms with the HIP worker (x16 link), 13.4 ms with the CUDA worker (x8 link, 2026-10-14 hip-cuda 8K trace)
worker.source_loopback: tools/glm_mixed_worker_loopback.py 2026-10-14: ownership_noop p50 42/40 us (cuda/hip); decode_partial width 2: cuda 105 us at 1 route, 500 us at 16; hip 157 / 396 us. Bounce 128 KB round trip 47/46 us; HostRegister on a shared memfd works on both vendors, also concurrently (6.95 / 13.9 GB/s).
